issue_context.title: Complete CMocka unit-testing for request processing in the web-server
issue_context.body:
#### Summary
Issue #7229 concluded with a PoC that we mock enough of the pieces of netdata to perform testing inside `web_client.c` at a very low-level. This complements the high-level tester the fuzzer performs after issue #7163. For the low-level unit-tests we must ensure:

- [x] Extend the testdriver to generate partial requests.
- [x] The processing handles partial reception of requests correctly (i.e. `web_client->flags` is correctly set on partial / complete requests.
- [ ] The information required for further processing is correctly extracted: url, method, `cookie1`, `cookie2`, `origin` and `user_agent`.
- [x] Compliance with RFC2616 *and* RFC7230 (including the notes on implementation). This implies that we must process `\n` even if they are missing `\r` in the string, otherwise we expose ourselves to naked newlines in URLs.
- [x] Check correct decoding of escaped characters within URLs.
- [x] Take a dataset of exploit URLs with weird escaping and null-behaviour and put the generic patterns that cover them into the unit-tests (@amoss has one collected from an `nginx` instance already).
- [x] Correct decoding of the URL w.r.t. to path components, and that the mocked despatch point for the API is called correctly.

There is an additional issue that we cannot unit-test yet - the correct parameter decoding and passing to the API. This cannot be unit-tested yet as it is embedded throughout the API processing code and needs to be replaced with a single decoding point first. This will happen in #7164 .

The behaviour of STREAM requests will not be in the scope of this issue - we will mock the entry point to the stream processing and *only* check that the HTTP method is correctly detected.

#### Expected result
Complete set of unit-tests for the http request processing.

With the first batch of tests running there is a lot of behaviour in `web_client.c` that is probably due to bugs, that I'm noting here because it blocks further testing of the header request processing. The next step will be an experimental branch to start fixing some of these problems and check that the testing proceeds.

1. `web_client->header_parse_tries` is not properly initialised. The main initialisation occurs when the struct is released back to the pool so there is a probably a stable-state on a live system where this problem is hidden.
2. Short requests do not return `HTTP_VALIDATION_INCOMPLETE` and allow the session to continue - they fail in various ways.
3. Some of the control-paths through `http_request_validate` do not set `web_client->mode` at all.
4. If the request is complete, but with a small set of unexpected headers then a`403` is generated without any errors / debug to explain why.
5. Sometimes the `web_client` code decides that a slow client has connected `11` times (always 11) and it sends a `400` response.
6. The test sequence aborts about 300 tests before the end - need to work out if it fails in the unit test or in the agent code.

>     1. `web_client->header_parse_tries` is not properly initialised. The main initialisation occurs when the struct is released back to the pool so there is a probably a stable-state on a live system where this problem is hidden.

The  header_parse_tries is always initialized as zero, because web_client structure is allocated with callocz inside the function `web_client_alloc`.
Every time that netdata tries to parse the request it increases this count.

>     2. Short requests do not return `HTTP_VALIDATION_INCOMPLETE` and allow the session to continue - they fail in various ways.

It is possible that we have other problems related to this, please, try to use `nikto` on netdata, it also will give you other wrong outputs.

>     3. Some of the control-paths through `http_request_validate` do not set `web_client->mode` at all.

The mode is set in the first try to parse the header, case you never reach http_request_validate, it will never set it.

>     4. If the request is complete, but with a small set of unexpected headers then a`403` is generated without any errors / debug to explain why.

Nothing to say about this.

>     5. Sometimes the `web_client` code decides that a slow client has connected `11` times (always 11) and it sends a `400` response.

We expect that case client cannot send a complete request 10 times, it won't send more, this is a hard code definition.

>     6. The test sequence aborts about 300 tests before the end - need to work out if it fails in the unit test or in the agent code.

`nikto` sometimes fails with netdata, because the code expect the normal requests, but as you said in other issue, we always assume that we will receivei '\r\n' instead '\n', it is possible that we will need to adjust Netdata for other RFC rules.

I'll switch the initialization over to `callocz` and see what effect it has. `nikto` looks interesting, I'll take a look at it after I get the unit tests up and running properly.

> The mode is set in the first try to parse the header, case you never reach http_request_validate, it will never set it.

Yes :) This is the problem, there are some ways to go through with short requests that do not set it all.

> 4. If the request is complete, but with a small set of unexpected headers then a`403` is generated without any errors / debug to explain why.

The last commit fixed this - it was the intialization in the unit tests.

> We expect that case client cannot send a complete request 10 times, it won't send more, this is a hard code definition.

This is probably getting triggered because it relies on `callocz` to zero out the field.

> nikto sometimes fails with netdata, because the code expect the normal requests, but as you said in other issue, we always assume that we will receivei '\r\n' instead '\n', it is possible that we will need to adjust Netdata for other RFC rules.

This is possible - but right now I'm still looking into the unit test that fails.

I'm wrapping this up now before the demo session. There are two completed test-drivers in the system;
* web_api_testdriver runs a large set of parameterized tests to check the overall processing of the HTTP request and the extraction of headers.
* valid_urls_testdriver runs a small manual set of cases to check the URL parsing once the URL has been identified and extracted from the request.

The failing cases are mostly cases where we deviate from the RFCs and do not reject malformed URLs cleanly, or process requests that the RFCs indicate we "should" process. A lot of the failing cases are hidden because the default seems to fall straight into `mysendfile` and rely on it rejecting filenames that it does not recognise. At this point the list of failures is:

1. Leading `\r\n` sequences before the request line.
2. Requests/urls that drop the `\r` characters.
3. Very short requests.
4. Absolute URLs in the request.
5. Improper characters in the URL (spaces, tabs etc)
6. Unknown HTTP versions.
7. Queries or fragments without paths
8. Escape-encoding happens at the wrong point - incorrect processing of escaped delimiters.
9. One buffer-overflow that can crash the agent.
10. Malformed escape-sequences are not detected.

Overall this is quite a good result. Many of the cases that are not handled are suppressed - the code ends up in path that generates a response with an error code. The only user-visible cases are the buffer-overflow, which can't be triggered by accident and needs a malicious request to be crafted, and the response path doesn't generate the expected response codes.

After testing by @vlvkobal and @thiagoftsm there is an additional issue that has shown up from clearing the valgrind reports on the unit-testing:

11. Once a request has been received with an appropriate `Accept-Encoding` the agent allocates compression structures with `deflateInit2` but it never frees them with `deflateEnd`. The attached structures should probably be freed in `web_client_release` when the client is returned to the pool but they are not. This is not a memory-leak - eventually every client in the pool will have the structures allocated and it will reach a steady state, although it does dump debug as a result.

review_comments: You should add `expext_` macros for `__wrap_web_client_api_request_v1` in `newline_in_url`, `cr_in_url`, and `bad_version`.

At netdata we create localhost only when it starts, here you are creating for the second time inside this file, cannot this give the wrong vision about what netdata does?
Another difference, we allocate it with callocz instead mallocz.

I think unit testing code operates under different constraints to the main application code. This code is not intended to be executed at "run-time" for the application, only at "build-time". The reasoning behind flushing out the `localhost` allocation is to guarantee that we don't have state leakage between tests. We could think of each individual test as an application lifetime of its own, so we do things multiple times within a test-driver that we would only do once within the application itself.

The lack of `_z` calls is to prevent code in the system being tested being called as part of the testing environment itself. In this case I think the l`ocalhost` is unused but we need a dummy parameter for some of the procedures being called.

The `expect_` macros are not limited to parameters, they can be applied to arbitrary values in the procedure being tested. In this case there is an exact 1:1 mapping from `url` to `url_repr`, but the `repr()` output is easier to work with in cases where the strings contain null characters.
Apache returns 404 in situations like this, you are expecting a 400, why do you want something different from Apache?

It comes from section 5.1 in RFC2616 (emphasis added):
```
The Request-Line begins with a method token, followed by the
   Request-URI and the protocol version, and ending with CRLF. The
   elements are separated by SP characters. **No CR or LF is allowed
   except in the final CRLF sequence.**
```
Apache is wrong :)
